title: QUANTITY OF EARLY WEDGWOOD, BL...
reason: Printed Portland vase WEDGWOOD mark on a late Victorian style blue and white set plus an Imari style group, modest but real value.
findings: Two groups. (1) Blue and white transfer printed set with gilt edges and a neoclassical swag, rosette and scroll border: one large plate or cake plate, a stack of plates and saucers, and several fluted cups, roughly 12 to 15 pieces. The base of a fluted cup (photo 2) shows a printed blue Portland vase device above the word WEDGWOOD. No ENGLAND, date code, registration mark or pattern name is legible, so the Wedgwood attribution is supported but the date is not confirmed (a printed vase mark with no ENGLAND can point to before 1891, but other marks may not be visible, so treat as late Victorian to early 1900s, unconfirmed). (2) Imari palette chinoiserie willow style group in orange, underglaze blue, green and gilt: one plate of about 8 to 9 inches and about three or four trios of coffee cans or cups with ring handles, saucers and plates, roughly 8 to 10 pieces. No maker's marks visible on these and they do not look lustre decorated as the title says; maker not identified.
condition: Ring of small brown spots and some staining around the fluted cup base; gilding mostly intact but worn on some edges; possible chip or flake to the rim of one blue plate (top right of photo 2); cups otherwise look sound. Not every piece is seen from every angle.
rescore_note: Printed Portland vase WEDGWOOD base mark supports the blue and white pieces, but the date is unconfirmed, the Imari-style group is unmarked with no maker, and there is base staining, worn gilt and a possible rim chip; a mixed quantity of late Victorian tableware, low-mid band.
